newsitem.title: SPAIN: Iberdrola says guarantees returns in difficult '97.
newsitem.headline: Iberdrola says guarantees returns in difficult '97.

text.p: The chairman of Spanish electrical utility Iberdrola said late on Wednesday he guaranteed shareholder returns.
Inigo de Oriol told reporters: "we have a surplus of 77.0 billion pesetas to guarantee shareholder returns".

"This will be a difficult year, although we hope to improve on first quarter results," he added, attributing a 5.3 percent fall in first quarter earnings to an asset revaluation programme and an unusually warm winter.
Oriol stressed the new investment plans of the firm, especially in Latin America. However "we'll look for growth and yield," he added.

Electrical sector liberalisation, which takes place as of January 1998 if parliament gives the draft final approval, will allow some clients of Iberdrola -- now 9.1 percent of its turnover -- to choose among electricity provider.
This will affect 20 percent of Iberdrola's turnover by the year 2001.

On Saturday, Iberdrola will hold its 1996 shareholders meeting. Iberdrola had provisional net profit of 96.64 billion pesetas in 1996, a rise of 13.7 percent on the previous year, and shareholders must approve the accounts.
